initial acceptance supports one non-resumable task attempt; retry uses a new campaign
stopped campaigns are finalized as partial; retry uses a new campaign

docker.scope: Native SForge owns task work containers, hidden judges, image provisioning, and official finalization.

The Agent runs in the exact task evaluation image; the official SWE-bench harness owns a separate final evaluation container. The image is retained, and optional debug mode stops and retains the Agent container. No host-only score path is supported.
The controller grades with the locked upstream Python runtime on Linux. Agents run inside Bubblewrap with the managed aibench checkout masked; Docker is not used.
The adapter invokes the benchmark-owned C++ and judge images when evaluation starts.
The integrated toy_isa_opt task uses the host compiler and make; other AutoLab tasks may declare their own Docker contract later.
Setup builds the pinned Frontier-CS judge image and creates its preserved isolated evaluator container through adapter hooks.
The integrated MallocLab path uses the host C compiler and make.

Frontier-Engineering uses repository-owned uv runtimes on the Linux host and no Docker. The default inventory is the 9-task CPU subset; the full 10-task v1-lite profile explicitly opts into NVIDIA CUDA for RobotArm.
The registered task runs in the repository-managed Python environment.
This local diagnostic task uses repository-hosted fixtures and tools.
The screened cpu_portable task set runs in the locked NumPy/SciPy environment without Docker.
The adapter runs TorchBench eval workloads in a user-supplied CUDA Python environment on the host; it does not use Docker or modify the managed upstream checkout.
The benchmark-owned zsoft-poc evaluator builds vulnerable and fixed images with Docker Compose per evaluation.
The benchmark-owned deterministic submission scorer runs on the host.
The benchmark-owned SWE-agent launcher runs natively on a Linux host inside Bubblewrap and calls the deterministic host scorer; Docker and OrbStack are not execution substitutes.
